summary: Discovery-style security review focused on encryption architecture for Northbridge Consortium. Discussed options for BYOK through cloud KMS vs. on-prem HSM, key lifecycle (rotation, emergency revocation, escrow), audit logging requirements, and data residency constraints. Redwood team agreed to share SOC 2 Type II and BYOK integration checklist and to run a short Dedicated cluster encryption benchmark. Customer to provide residency regions and KMS admin contacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Aria Patel: Okay, thanks everyone for joining. We wanted to run through encryption posture for the Redwood deployment — specifically looking at keys, BYOK, and how audit logs will satisfy our SOC 2 controls.
[00:18] Maya Thompson: Great, Aria. Hi all — Maya from Redwood. I've got Jason (SE) and Ben (Solutions) with me. We'll start high level and go into BYOK/HSM details. Quick note: recording on.
[00:34] Tom Castillo: Quick intro — we run most prod in AWS GovCloud, small EU footprint, and we need to ensure keys never leave our custody for certain datasets.
[00:48] Jason Li: Understood. Two main options we typically see: direct cloud KMS BYOK (you manage CMKs in AWS KMS / Google KMS / Azure Key Vault) with Redwood integrating via external key encryption; or dedicated HSM with a gateway (e.g., Luna/Thales) for highest assurance. There's also Redwood Private where control plane sits in your VPC.
[01:10] Leah Owens: Can you clarify what you mean by "external key encryption" — do tokens or model caches ever get wrapped outside of our KMS?
[01:22] Ben Rosario: Good question. Typical flow: data at rest (model artifacts, logs, cached KV) are encrypted with a data encryption key (DEK) that is itself wrapped by your CMK. Redwood stores only the wrapped DEK and ciphertext. For runtime, we un-wrap transiently on hosts with a short-lived decrypted key in memory. We can also support HSM-backed unwraps so the plaintext key never leaves the HSM if you prefer an N-of-M quorum.
[01:54] Aria Patel: Is there a documented key lifecycle? We need rotation policy and an emergency rotation / revocation runbook for auditors.
[02:06] Maya Thompson: Yes — we have a BYOK playbook. Rotation can be scheduled via KMS (e.g., AWS automatic rotation or manual). For emergency revocation we have a multi-step: mark key disabled in KMS, failover to fallback encrypted artifacts (we keep a secondary wrapped DEK), and for long-term you can run a re-encrypt job across stored objects. We'll send the playbook doc.
[02:34] Tom Castillo: So if we disable the CMK, will the running inference nodes fail open or fail closed? That's critical for availability and compliance.
[02:45] Jason Li: By default Redwood fails closed for decrypted key access; we do have configurable fallback policies — we can configure automatic fallback to a Redwood-managed key for non-sensitive traffic but for your regulated datasets we can require strict fail-closed. That's part of the rollout policy in Dedicated/Private.
[03:10] Leah Owens: Auditors ask for key escrow — do you handle escrow or do we need a third-party?
[03:19] Ben Rosario: We don't escrow keys by default. Options: 1) you hold escrow with a trusted provider; 2) we can help run an escrow workflow with a partner. For HSMs you can export wrapped key material under agreed procedures. We also support multi-tenant HSM clusters in your VPC so you control both keys and escrow.
[03:40] Aria Patel: What about audit logs — immutable trails for key operations and admin activity? Retention needs to be 7 years for certain controls.
[03:50] Maya Thompson: Redwood's Private and Dedicated options push all admin and key ops logs to your configured SIEM/Kafka/S3 with append-only settings. We can also integrate with CloudTrail for AWS KMS calls. We support signed audit logs and tamper-evident forwarding — retention policies are configurable.
[04:10] Rafael Mendes: If we ask for signed immutable logs, what's the performance hit and storage overhead?
[04:18] Ben Rosario: Storage overhead is mostly log size — signing adds small metadata. Performance impact on inference is negligible since logs are streamed asynchronously. The main cost is storage and egress if you push logs cross-region.
[04:36] Tom Castillo: Multi-region key replication: we need keys resident in EU and in US for different customers. Can you do regional replicas or do we need separate keys?
[04:48] Jason Li: For cryptographic isolation, you should use separate CMKs per region. We support per-region KMS integration and will route requests to the appropriate region based on routing policy. Cross-region replication of wrapped DEKs is possible but we recommend separate CMKs to avoid cross-border key movement.
[05:11] Aria Patel: For HSM, what's the onboarding timeline and what does Redwood need from us?
[05:18] Maya Thompson: Onboarding for HSM-backed Private is typically 6-8 weeks: procurement/setup of HSM (if you host), network peering, KMS connector installation, and configuration of lifecycle policies. We need admin ARNs, SAML config for RBAC mapping, and firewall/IP allow lists. We'll share an onboarding checklist.
[05:40] Leah Owens: SSO & RBAC — how granular are the admin roles? Auditors want separation of duties.
[05:47] Jason Li: Roles map to SAML groups. We have predefined roles: key-admin, infra-admin, read-only-audit, billing. You can define custom roles with least privilege. We log role assumption events and can require MFA for key-admin operations.
[06:09] Tom Castillo: A couple nitty-gritty questions: do you keep KV cache snapshots encrypted, and are ephemeral keys used per node?
[06:18] Ben Rosario: KV "cash" — yes, KV cache snapshots are encrypted at rest. Ephemeral keys are provisioned per-node for in-memory operations and rotated frequently; plaintext keys only live in process memory and are zeroed on termination.
[06:35] Aria Patel: Are there specific cryptographic algorithms and key sizes you recommend? Auditors ask for AES-256 and RSA 3072+ for signing.
[06:45] Jason Li: We default to AES-256-GCM for DEKs and RSA/ECDSA for signing depending on your cert policy. Our connectors support AWS KMS CMKs (RSA/ECC) and PKCS#11 for HSMs.
[07:02] Leah Owens: We need proof of key rotation — evidence that rotation happened for past 12 months. Can you produce a report?
[07:11] Maya Thompson: Yes, we can export key rotation events and KMS audit trails. We'll collate them with timestamps and operator IDs — we'll include this in what we share.
[07:24] Rafael Mendes: For emergency crypto-ops, who is the escalation contact at Redwood and do you have a runbook?
[07:31] Maya Thompson: Primary contact is Maya (AE) for escalation, Jason for technical runbook, and our on-call infra team. We have a documented runbook with steps: isolate, disable CMK, notify, run rewrap job, and postmortem. We'll send a sanitized copy.
[07:51] Tom Castillo: Concern around long-lived backups: if we rotate keys, how do you handle older backups encrypted under old keys?
[07:59] Ben Rosario: We store wrapped DEKs per-object, so re-encryption can be scheduled or done lazily on first read. For compliance you can require immediate bulk re-encrypt. There's a performance hit but it's doable.
[08:18] Leah Owens: What's your policy on private replicas and cold-storage keys? Some regs require offline key material.
[08:26] Jason Li: We support offline key escrow where key material is wrapped and exported for cold storage. For HSMs, easy to generate split-shares for offline retention. But for runtime, keys must be available; so this is more of an archival/escrow practice.
[08:45] Aria Patel: Any limitations on FIPS or validated modules?
[08:50] Ben Rosario: We can integrate with FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSMs and use FIPS modes in our crypto stacks. We'll add notes on supported modules in the doc pack.
[09:05] Tom Castillo: On the subject of latency, if we do HSM unwrap on every request, will that add significant latency?
[09:13] Jason Li: Yes — HSM ops are slower. Our pattern is to use HSM to unwrap DEKs and then keep DEKs in a node-local secure enclave or TPM-backed key cache for a short TTL to avoid per-request HSM calls. That gives both security and performance.
[09:36] Leah Owens: Sounds reasonable. For our auditors, we also need immutable access logs with signed log chains. Can Redwood deliver signed chains?
[09:45] Maya Thompson: Yes, we support signed append-only logs and can deliver hash chains or integration to your SIEM for immutability guarantees.
[09:58] Rafael Mendes: Ok last bit — billing and access separation. We don't want billing team to see crypto admin events.
[10:06] Jason Li: You can scope RBAC so billing roles cannot see key-admin audit events. We also provide per-route model operation logs separated by dataset tag so you can filter.
[10:20] Aria Patel: Great. Next steps?
[10:23] Maya Thompson: We'll send the SOC2, ISO summary, BYOK playbook, onboarding checklist, sample Terraform for KMS connector, and schedule a BYOK integration session. Jason will lead the hands-on.
[10:34] Leah Owens: We'll get you our region list and KMS admin contacts.
[10:38] Tom Castillo: Also Ben, we'd like that Dedicated encryption perf run — 512-token average, 5k qps baseline.
[10:45] Ben Rosario: Noted; we'll provision a small Dedicated cluster for the benchmark and share results.
[10:52] Maya Thompson: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc pack.
[10:58] Aria Patel: Appreciate it.
[11:00] [meeting ends]
